## What's Been Implemented

✅ **Full OAuth 2.0 Support** including:
- Client Credentials Flow (server-to-server authentication)
- Automatic token refresh when tokens expire
- Built-in support for Microsoft Graph API
- SAP OIDC endpoint configuration
- Comprehensive error handling and fallback mechanisms

## How to Use OAuth with OData MCP

### Configuration Options

You can configure OAuth using environment variables or command-line arguments:

#### Environment Variables
```bash
export OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="your-client-id"
export OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET="your-client-secret"
export OAUTH_TOKEN_URL="https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token"
export OAUTH_SCOPE="https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"  # Optional
```

#### Command Line
```bash
python odata_mcp.py \
    --service https://your-sap-service.com/odata/ \
    --oauth-client-id YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
    --oauth-client-secret YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \
    --oauth-token-url https://your-sap.com/sap/bc/sec/oauth2/token \
    --oauth-scope "odata_read odata_write"
```

### SAP-Specific Configuration

For SAP backends with OIDC configuration (as mentioned in your referenced documentation), you can use:

```bash
python odata_mcp.py \
    --service https://your-sap-system.com:8443/sap/opu/odata/sap/YOUR_SERVICE/ \
    --oauth-client-id YOUR_SAP_CLIENT_ID \
    --oauth-client-secret YOUR_SAP_CLIENT_SECRET \
    --oauth-token-url https://your-sap-system.com:8443/sap/bc/sec/oauth2/token \
    --oauth-scope "odata_read odata_write" \
    --verbose
```

The implementation follows the authorization code flow pattern you suggested, where:
1. Token is obtained using client credentials
2. Token is automatically included as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header
3. Tokens are automatically refreshed when they expire
